name: Hardy Reef
description: Hardy Reef on the outer Great Barrier Reef off the Whitsundays, with Heart Reef, the Reefworld pontoon and the neighbouring Hook, Line and Bait reefs, rebuilt from 30 m survey bathymetry and Sentinel-2. The site has no land: you start in the water beside the pontoon.
area_note: Hardy Reef with the reefs around it: Hook Reef across the channel, Line Reef to the north and Bait Reef to the west. The first config ran 6 km further south over open water 40-80 m deep; it now stops 3 km south of Hook Reef and takes in all of Line Reef and Bait Reef instead.

imagery.attribution: Contains modified Copernicus Sentinel-2 data (ESA, Copernicus open licence), via Earth Search on AWS

terrain.attribution: AusSeabed / Geoscience Australia, Great Barrier Reef Bathymetry 2020 30 m (not for navigation)

start.note: over Hardy Reef south-east of Heart Reef, looking north-west across Heart Reef's pool toward the channel and Reefworld; Heart Reef itself is two or three pixels of the 10 m imagery and is not resolved as a heart

spawn.note: the site has no land: on the deck of the Reefworld pontoon (the viewer puts the player there; x, y are the fallback in the water off its south end, about 15 m deep on the 30 m model)

pois.name: Reefworld
pois.note: tour pontoon permanently moored at Hardy Reef (Cruise Whitsundays); on the 30 m model it sits on the top of the reef wall, 8.6 m deep, with 32 m of water 60 m to the west

pois.name: Heart Reef
pois.note: a heart-shaped coral formation within Hardy Reef, first spotted by a local pilot in 1975; protected, no swimming or snorkelling at the formation; best seen from the air.

pois.name: Toward Airlie Beach and the Whitsunday Islands

poi_sources.osm: OpenStreetMap contributors (ODbL): the point Nominatim returns for the object, which for a reef way is a point on its surface (read 2026-10-28; the same objects are in Overture Maps 2026-10-21.0 base land and infrastructure). The `osm` field names the object.
poi_sources.nominal: chosen for the viewer; the boats search near it for water 5-9 m deep
poi_sources.not mapped: the channel between Hardy and Hook reefs and the lagoon inside Hardy Reef have no name in OpenStreetMap or Overture, so they are not POIs. OSM also has a node 'Hardy Reef Pontoon' (node 5611360021, tourism=attraction) 1 km east of Reefworld on the reef flat (2-3 m deep); which pontoon it stands for is not stated, so it is left out.

pontoon.name: Reefworld
pontoon.note: exact: put the pontoon on its mapped position instead of searching for 9-18 m water (the reef wall drops from 9 to 32 m within 60 m, so the search finds nothing on this side of the channel). heading 180: long side along the north-south reef wall, day boat on the starboard (west) side over the channel, helipad astern to the north

tide.note: Bugatti Reef (MSQ standard port, 20 05 S 150 18 E) is on the outer reef about 120 km east-south-east of Reefworld; MSQ publishes no tide for Hardy Reef. It is used rather than Shute Harbour (73 km south-west, on the mainland) because Hardy, like Bugatti, is an outer reef in open water: MSQ's 2026 tidal planes give a spring range (MHWS - MLWS) of 2.08 m at Bugatti Reef, 2.77 m at Shute Harbour and 2.4 m at Hook Island, the nearest listed place (44 km south-west of Hardy, inside the island group). Times and heights at Hardy Reef differ from Bugatti's by amounts MSQ does not publish.

life.note: No land: no plants. Spawning: an outer reef of the central Great Barrier Reef (Willis et al. 1985 (researchonline.jcu.edu.au/24208): the offshore mass spawning period is one lunar month after the inshore one; Peter Harrison in Australian Geographic, 'Synchronised sex', 9 May 2016: the periods after the full moon in October and November for the inshore reefs, and November and December for the offshore and northern and southern reefs), lag 1.
